The trip was a RydeTAXI job (metered): total charged $25.26 made up of base $3.90, distance $14.95 for 10.60 km, time $4.83, waiting $0.11 and platform $1.47 [F7]. One off-route segment exists, 14:28–14:34: 3.07 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.12 km, adding 1.94 km [F3], and under RD-1 every such segment must be tested against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5, with no percentage or absolute-km threshold [F1][F3][RD-1].

No traffic justification exempts that segment: the trace settles that no incident was reported on the replaced stretch, and the record shows no incident near the route at all [F15][RD-4]; the only congestion evidence is AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 14:10–14:28 [F12], which under RD-4(b) is at most corroboration and cannot exempt a segment on its own [F12][RD-4].

RD-5 is where the case turns, and the rider's own message cannot get there on timing. The rider's only message, "Sure, no problem.", was sent at 14:31 [F9], while the segment it is said to authorise had already begun at 14:28 [F3]. The driver's post-trip statement that he told the rider beforehand [F11] is a statement, not rider consent, and cannot substitute for a rider message sent before the segment [F11][RD-5].

The driver is not left without an arguable reading: his 14:30 message names a specific road, "go round via Clementi Road" [F8], and the rider's "Sure, no problem." [F9] is on its face an agreement — and because 14:31 falls inside the 14:28–14:34 segment window, part of the segment is arguably covered [F3][F9][RD-5]. But even taking the driver's reading, the record never ties the driven 14:28–14:34 path to Clementi Road, and the agreed stretch cannot be matched to what was driven on timing alone [F3][F8][F10][RD-5]. The trace records that this finding changes the amount, so the whole 1.94 km must either be exempt or refunded. The rider's complaint that she said "sure" only because the car was already on the new route matches the timestamps, and the balance of the record favours her on this point [F3][F8][F9][F11][RD-5]. No rider-named stop excuses the segment: the chat contains only a route question and a one-word reply, with no place named by the rider and no stop measured in the segment [F3][F8][F9][F10][RD-3].
